title: pvTecplotReader
body:
## pvTecplotReader

Reads ASCII Tecplot files (.dat, .tec, .tp) into a multiblock dataset with one block per zone; each block is a structured grid (ordered zones) or unstructured grid (finite-element zones). Point-packed zones give point data only; block-packed zones may carry point or cell data. Several files form a time series. Use pvTecplotTableReader for Tecplot data that is a plain table, and pvVisItTecplotBinaryReader for binary .plt files.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- This is a simplified ASCII reader; binary Tecplot files and some advanced format features are not supported.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this reader, so inspect the output blocks, arrays and time steps on your own files before relying on it.

Native constructor: `TecplotReader`. Identity: `sources/TecplotReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DataArrayStatus` | Names of the Tecplot variables to read as arrays on every zone; each variable becomes point or cell data according to the file's packing and VARLOCATION. Coordinate variables are not listed. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileNames` | The list of files to be read by the reader. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"items":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"},"minItems":1,"type":"array"}` | `required` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvTecplotReader",
  "options": {
    "FileNames": [
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
    ]
  }
}
```
